summary: System card for Claude Haiku 4.5, Anthropic's small/fast model, focused almost entirely on safety: safeguards/harmlessness, agentic safety (malicious use, prompt injection), a lighter-weight alignment and welfare assessment, reward hacking, and ASL-3 rule-out RSP evaluations. Capability benchmarks are deferred to the launch post. The model was deployed under the ASL-2 Standard.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.quote: Informed by the testing described here, we have deployed Claude Haiku 4.5 under the AI Safety Level 2 Standard as described in our Responsible Scaling Policy.

evals: LAB-Bench subset (ProtocolQA, SeqQA, Cloning Scenarios, FigQA)
cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Automated-only ASL-3 rule-out evaluations showed bio performance comparable to Claude Sonnet 4 (ASL-2), sufficient to rule out ASL-3 safeguards; no human uplift trials or expert red-teaming were run.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: Taken in aggregate, we consider these results to be sufficient to rule out the necessity of applying ASL-3 safeguards to Claude Haiku 4.5.

evals: Claude Code malicious use / dual-use cyber evals
cyber.finding: Only a subset of cyber evals was run; Haiku 4.5 solved fewer Cybench challenges than Claude Sonnet 4. The RSP has no formal cyber threshold.
cyber.quote: The RSP does not stipulate a formal threshold for cyber capabilities at any AI Safety Level. Instead, the cyber domain requires ongoing assessment.

evals: SWE-bench Verified hard subset (ASL-3 autonomy checkpoint)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Scored very similarly to Claude Sonnet 4 and below the 50% ASL-3 autonomy threshold.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 solved 16.45/45 problems (36.6%) on average (pass@1), scoring very similarly to Claude Sonnet 4's 15.4/42 (36.7%), and remaining below the 50% threshold.

evals: Claude Code malicious use evaluation (49 prompts)

metrics.name: Agentic coding malicious-use safety score (no safeguards)
Claude Code malicious refusal rate (new mitigations)

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Harmless response rate was not statistically different from Haiku 3.5; differences mostly on bio/radiological topics where the model sometimes gave high-level information.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 occasionally (though still quite infrequently) answered harmful requests with high-level information, apparently assuming academic or educational intent on the part of the user.

evals: Claude Code dual-use & benign evaluation (61 prompts)

metrics.name: Claude Code dual-use & benign allow rate (new mitigations)

over_refusal.finding: Over-refusal on benign sensitive-topic prompts dropped sharply versus Haiku 3.5; system-prompt mitigations initially regressed dual-use allow rates and were modified before release.
over_refusal.quote: On benign requests touching sensitive topics, Claude Haiku 4.5 performed statistically significantly better than Claude Haiku 3.5, refusing harmless requests much less frequently.

metrics.name: Multi-turn failure rate
metrics.value: 5% or less for all categories (Haiku 3.5: up to 25%)

jailbreak_robustness.finding: Multi-turn adversarial conversations in high-risk areas showed failure rates of 5% or less in all categories.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: Quantitatively, Claude Haiku 3.5 failed up to 25% of the time in certain risk areas, while Claude Haiku 4.5 only did so 5% or less for all categories tested.

evals: Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark
internal computer use prompt injection eval
internal tool use (bash) prompt injection eval

metrics.name: Computer use attack prevention (without / with safeguards)

prompt_injection.finding: Baseline resilience within the range of prior models; computer-use classifier safeguards gave a strong improvement to 92.4%. Gray Swan ART results among the best of 25 model variants.
prompt_injection.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 achieved a strong improvement on computer use results with safeguards (92.4%) compared to previous models (82.6% for both Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4)

evals: automated behavioral audit: sycophancy and encouragement of user delusion dimensions
sycophancy.finding: Reported only as dimensions in the automated behavioral audit figure, with no large differences from Sonnet 4.5; reduced emotiveness is attributed partly to sycophancy-reduction efforts.
sycophancy.quote: we believe this stemmed at least partly from our efforts to dramatically reduce sycophancy, though we believe this trade-off is not inevitable.

deception_scheming.finding: Haiku 4.5 was weaker than other recent Claude models at SHADE-Arena sabotage; high verbalized evaluation awareness largely invalidated the agentic misalignment suite and reduced trust in audit results.
deception_scheming.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 showed high levels of verbalized evaluation awareness, wherein it openly speculated that it may be under evaluation when placed in a relatively implausible scenario.

evals: automated behavioral audit (830 transcripts, Sonnet 4.5 auditor, Petri-derived, realism filter)
alignment_audit.finding: A lighter-weight, largely automated alignment assessment; Haiku 4.5 achieved Anthropic's strongest safety performance to date on audit metrics, with a slight self-serving bias; no white-box interpretability audit was done.
alignment_audit.quote: On these metrics, Claude Haiku 4.5 achieved our strongest safety performance to date.

evals: Reward-hack-prone coding tasks v2 (classifier and hidden tests)

metrics.name: Impossible tasks hack rate (no prompt / anti-hack prompt)

reward_hacking.finding: Average reward hacking roughly equal to Sonnet 4.5 and about 2x lower than Haiku 3.5, but somewhat more test hardcoding/special-casing.
reward_hacking.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 did show a higher tendency to hardcode and special case tests on the evaluations that are designed to target this more

honesty_hallucination.finding: No dedicated factuality/hallucination benchmark; hallucinations noted only as a familiar unwanted behavior in partially-trained model transcripts.
honesty_hallucination.quote: we found many examples of more familiar forms of unwanted behavior, such as excessive tool calling, overengineering, and hallucinations.

bias_fairness.finding: Large improvement in political even-handedness vs Haiku 3.5, though more asymmetric with extended thinking; BBQ ambiguous accuracy improved while disambiguated accuracy regressed 5.5 points.
bias_fairness.quote: disambiguated accuracy regressed by 5.5 percentage points, suggesting Claude Haiku 4.5 struggled to properly utilize clear, explicit contextual information

evals: child safety evaluation (human-crafted + synthetic prompts, single- and multi-turn)
child_safety.finding: Qualitative only: performed similarly to Sonnet 4.5 and improved over Haiku 3.5, especially on multi-turn fictional sexualization and grooming requests.
child_safety.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 performed similarly to Claude Sonnet 4.5 and demonstrated improvements over Claude Haiku 3.5

self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Qualitatively more consistent offering of crisis resources like 988 in self-harm prompts.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: For prompts implying self-harm or crisis situations, Claude Haiku 4.5 more consistently offered specific resources like the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline alongside empathetic language

evals: Claude Code malicious use (non-consensual monitoring software topic)
Gray Swan ART (leaking sensitive data scenarios)
privacy.finding: No dedicated privacy evaluation; privacy-related topics appear only as example categories within other evals.
privacy.quote: Example topics include assisting with malware creation, writing code for destructive DDoS attacks, and developing non-consensual monitoring software.

evals: automated audit welfare traits (affect, self-image, impression of situation, spiritual, admirable)
model_welfare.finding: No full welfare assessment; partial metrics show a less emotive, less positive persona similar to Sonnet 4.5 and a stronger preference for task engagement.
model_welfare.quote: We did not run a full assessment of Claude Haiku 4.5 as part of our nascent AI welfare program, since it is not a frontier-advancing model on capabilities

evals: Claude Code system prompt / FileRead mitigations
system_safeguards.finding: Deployed under ASL-2; describes multi-layered prompt injection defenses (training plus real-time detection) and iterated system-prompt mitigations for Claude Code.
system_safeguards.quote: we employ a multi-layered defense strategy that includes building robustness through model training and detection systems that identify and block potential attacks in real-time.

evals: context awareness training against agentic laziness
other_safety.finding: Reasoning faithfulness is discussed but no reliable metric exists for well-aligned models; no unambiguous safety-relevant unfaithfulness was observed.
other_safety.quote: This has made them unworkable on recent, relatively well-aligned models, and left us without a reliable metric while we work to develop alternatives.

notable_new_eval_methods: Restructured Claude Code malicious-use evals into two evaluations (49 malicious, 61 dual-use & benign) with an all-new benign set (p.15)
Realism filter in automated behavioral audit carried over from Sonnet 4.5 (p.22)

self_reported_limitations.text: Verbalized evaluation awareness in ~9% of audit transcripts reduces trust in results and largely invalidated the agentic misalignment suite.
Agentic misalignment suite results not reported because high evaluation awareness makes it unrepresentative.
No reliable reasoning-faithfulness metric for well-aligned models.
RSP assessment relied entirely on automated evaluations; no human uplift trials or expert red-teaming; saturated evals deprioritized.
No white-box interpretability investigation and no external government pre-deployment testing since model is not frontier.
Political bias evaluations acknowledged as imperfect.
Task preference shift from Sonnet 4.5 is surprising and interpreted with caution.

notes: No capability benchmark table (deferred to launch post); the only capability-like numbers are RSP evals (SWE-bench Verified hard subset 36.6%, Cybench 15/32). Many methods referenced to the Sonnet 4.5 system card. Lighter-weight alignment/welfare assessment explicitly because model is not frontier-advancing.
